findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O errors (file not found, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted filesystem input causes uncontrolled panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain error enum) and propagate the error with ?

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println) with parsing logic. The entire function is imperative shell, not a pure core.
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test parsing logic without filesystem access; parsing is coupled to side effects
findings.fix: Split into: (1) shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> that reads the file and delegates to (2) a pure fn parse_sessions(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: println!() in what should be a parsing function — hidden I/O side effect in core-adjacent code
findings.failure_mode: side effects leak into the data-processing layer, making it untestable and unpredictable; logging must be in the shell
findings.fix: Remove println!; if logging is needed, return enriched records or let the shell layer handle logging after parsing

findings.problem: Uses split(',').map(...).collect() then indexes into the collected Vec, instead of split_once or get for fixed-field parsing
findings.failure_mode: allocates a full Vec of strings only to access two fields; also creates unchecked indexing risk on the next line
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError) to extract name and value fields without collecting

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with fewer than 2 fields causes index-out-of-bounds panic instead of a typed parse error

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with exactly one field causes index-out-of-bounds panic
non-numeric value in the value field causes uncontrolled panic instead of returning a typed parse error

findings.problem: as u16 — lossy width cast from u32 to u16, silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536..u32::MAX silently wrap to incorrect u16 values, corrupting data
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_value).map_err(ParseError::Overflow) instead of as u16; parse directly to u16 if the field is always u16-range

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve before collecting lines from file input (unbounded capacity)
findings.failure_mode: large input files can exhaust memory with no graceful handling; Vec::with_capacity is not used and allocation failure is not mapped to a typed error
findings.fix: Pre-populate a Vec with a reasonable reserve (or known bound) using try_reserve, or parse into a pre-allocated structure and propagate allocation errors

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string is imperative I/O in a function that returns a domain data type (Vec<Record>) — the core contains shell logic
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic cannot be tested in isolation; callers cannot supply test data without creating temp files
findings.fix: Extract a pure parse_sessions(&str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> function for the core; shell wraps it with fs::read_to_string and error context

findings.problem: Record has pub fields with String — domain data should be validated at the boundary, not allow arbitrary string content
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct Record with invalid names, bypassing invariants; violates 'illegal states unrepresentable'
findings.fix: Use a newtype or make fields private with a fallible constructor that validates name is non-empty and value is in range

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any claimed throughput or latency of load_sessions
no profiler data exists to show allocation profile of the split+collect+map pipeline
no allocation audit (e.g., cargo-bench with --bench-threads=1, or heaptrack) for the Vec growth path
no second-ring evidence (e.g., kani, miri) for the unsafe indexing and unwrap paths on malformed input
no CLI/command harness or integration test exercising the full I/O pipeline
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. The crate has 11 BLOCKER findings spanning unwrap() calls, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, I/O in core, missing try_reserve, and no evidence. All must be addressed before delivery.
